summary: The unit is a sound, complete translation of four short paragraphs; every word is glossed and the Hebrew-letter and phrase checks hold. Faults: 2:19 left the 'lowly to the honoured' clause without a main clause and misrendered 'men of understanding' (Job 34:10) and 'from the commandments'; 2:20 renders עבודה אחרת two ways and splits 'kneel and bow down'; 2:21 mistranslates the weqatal verb of 1 Kgs 19:18 ('Yet I have left') and adds 'then' for הוא. Several allusions (Gen 15:6, Job 34:10, Job 23:12, Job 6:18, Eccl 7:14) were not recognised.

patches.value: The first: there is a great difference between one who worships and prays to something, and one who only honours something. To pray to something and to worship something with worship is forbidden to us, whether it be a man or an angel, corporeal or spiritual; but to bestow honour, as a youth honours an elder, a servant his master, and the lowly the honoured, is permitted. So too we find of our father Abraham, who believed in the LORD, that he shattered the monuments of idols and disowned them, and bowed down to the ground before three angels standing over him, even though they appeared to him as men. So too Joshua did at Jericho: when he saw a man standing before him and took him for an angel, he fell to the ground before him. And if men of understanding like them, in whose ways we walk and from the commandments of whose lips we do not shrink, did this, and it was not counted to them as a sin of idolatry; it is clear that to honour a Torah scroll is not the worship of idols.
patches.reason: The second half of the contrast has no main clause ('it is permitted for the lowly to the honoured' adds 'it' and 'for'; the Hebrew's subject is the infinitive לחלוק כבוד with its three examples, and מותר is its predicate). Also: 'idol-monuments' is an invented compound for מצבות אלילים (construct); אנשי לבב is Job 34:10, 'men of understanding' (the verse's sense governs, per the allusion ruling); 'whose commandments of their lips' is ungrammatical and מ in וממצות is 'from'.

patches.value: נבוש: 'we are ashamed / shrink from'. Question: the phrase echoes Job 23:12, 'מצות שפתיו ולא אמיש' (I have not departed from the commandment of His lips); the author may intend נמוש, 'we depart'. 'Shrink from' fits both; the printed word is translated and the alternative recorded in apparatus.
patches.reason: Decisions have a ruling for a printed word close to a likelier one (יכינו for יבינו): proposed ruling, translate by the sense, give printed word and likelier in token note and apparatus. Owner to confirm נבוש/נמוש.

patches.value: Second: the Jews are very careful in matters of other worship, and even to appear as one who honours it is forbidden to them. As they said in the Talmud and in the Rambam: "If a man turned aside from the road he was taking near a house of idolatry, and a thorn lodged in his foot, he may not bend, nor even kneel and bow down to remove it there, so that he should not appear in the eyes of passers-by as one who bows down and honours idolatry." And if the prostration before the Ark were like other worship, the Jews would not have kept this custom; and since they kept it from the days of their fathers, it is a sign of truth that it is not corrupted.
patches.reason: 'עבודה אחרת' is rendered 'other worship' in the first sentence and 'worship of another kind' in the second: same phrase, same English. Also 'nor bow down' makes a third negated verb; the Hebrew is 'nor even kneel and bow down' (אף לא יכרע וישתחוה).

patches.reason: Literal in Hebrew order: 'nor not' for אף לא; 'other' for אחרת; ארחות is 'paths'.
אף is 'even'; it was glossed 'nor'.
אחרת is 'other'; the gloss 'of another kind' differs from 2:20.7.

patches.value: עבודה אחרת: 'other worship', the Talmudic euphemism for idolatry (עבודה זרה). Proposed ruling: render 'other worship' every time, as with אל אחר 'another god', so that the euphemism shows.
patches.reason: Decisions are silent on עבודה אחרת.

value: כמו שאמרו בתלמוד וברמב"ם: the formula אמרו introduces the passage that follows, which is therefore in quotation marks; no reference is given.
לא ישח אף לא יכרע וישתחוה להוציאו: the negative governs all three verbs: he may not stoop, nor even kneel and bow down; the clause 'so that he should not appear' gives the reason.
ואם היתה ... לא היו היהודים מחזיקים: a counterfactual, both clauses in the past; the author argues from what the Jews would not have done.
וכיון שהחזיקו בו מימי אבותיהם אות אמת הוא כי אינה משובשת: the argument from custom; 'since they kept it' is causal, and 'that it is not corrupted' gives the sign's content.
patches.reason: The note said 'two negated' of three verbs, and described the quoted passage as given in the author's own wording, which the pack does not establish.

value: Job 6:18: cf. 'ילפתו ארחות דרכם' (they turn aside the paths of their way), the source of the wording לפת ארחות דרכו.
The author names no tractate or chapter for the Talmud and Rambam passage.
patches.reason: Allusion recognised; the earlier line asserted 'paraphrase', which the pack does not show.

patches.value: Third: one of the customs of honour by which they once honoured idolatry was kissing. So too we find in Scripture: "And I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him." And it is said: "Those who sacrifice men kiss calves." And if it is so, will all who kiss the Torah scroll be worshippers of idols? But the matter is not so, for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah, and not worship; and therefore the prostration before the Ark is also only honour and not worship.
patches.reason: 1 Kgs 19:18: והשארתי is weqatal, 'and I will leave'; 'Yet' and 'I have left' are not in the Hebrew. ואם כן הוא is 'and if it is so': the translation drops 'and' and 'it is'.

value: וכן מצינו במקרא: the verse is 1 Kgs 19:18, quoted in the words of the verse; 'we find' introduces it without a formula.

ונאמר זובחי אדם עגלים ישקון: the second verse, Hos 13:2, with the spelling זובחי (the verse has זבחי); the subject is the sacrificers and ישקון is the plural imperfect, 'kiss' (or, as a wish, 'let them kiss').
ואם כן הוא יהיו כל המנשקים ... עובדי ע"ז?: a question about the future, answered by 'but this is not so'.
כי אין זה רק כבוד שיכבדו את תורתם ולא עבודה: 'for this is only honour, that they honour their Torah and not worship' explains 'this'.
patches.reason: The old note said the 1 Kgs verse was in the author's wording as if it differed; it is verbatim. Hos 13:2 spelling not recorded.

value: 1 Kgs 19:18: quoted in the verse's own words.
